inline_comments.comment: `self.results['stress'] = stress` is stored unconditionally regardless of whether the system has a valid 3D cell. For a molecule or a 2D system, `compute_energy_and_forces` will compute stress using `volume = 1.0` as a fallback (see below), producing a physically meaningless result that is then silently reported to the caller. The assignment should be guarded: `if self.atoms.cell.rank == 3: self.results['stress'] = stress`, and no entry should be placed in `self.results` otherwise so that `get_stress()` raises `PropertyNotImplementedError` as expected.

Catching the bare `Exception` type is far too broad; it will silently swallow unexpected errors (e.g. memory errors, AttributeError, segfaults from the underlying calculator) and make debugging very difficult. The intent is clearly to handle the case where the underlying calculator does not implement stress. Use `PropertyNotImplementedError` from `ase.calculators.calculator` instead, which is the precise exception ASE calculators are required to raise in this case.

Setting `volume = 1.0` as a fallback when the system is not 3D-periodic causes the bias virial to be returned as-is (divided by 1) in Voigt form and stored as the stress, which is dimensionally incorrect and physically meaningless. Additionally, the condition `self.atoms.pbc.any() and self.atoms.cell.rank == 3` is too restrictive: a 3D cell with `pbc=[False, False, False]` (e.g. a cluster in a box) passes `cell.rank == 3` but fails `pbc.any()`, so the real cell volume would not be used. Stress computation (and any result storage) should be gated solely on `self.atoms.cell.rank == 3`, consistent with ASE conventions.

This manual 3×3 → Voigt conversion uses only one of each pair of symmetric off-diagonal elements (e.g. `virial_bias[1, 2]` alone instead of `(virial_bias[1, 2] + virial_bias[2, 1]) / 2`). ASE's canonical utility `full_3x3_to_voigt_6_stress` from `ase.stress` — which is already imported at the top of this file in the current codebase — correctly symmetrises each off-diagonal component. For a numerically asymmetric virial (possible under certain PLUMED actions), this manual extraction will give incorrect off-diagonal stress components. Replace the entire array construction with `full_3x3_to_voigt_6_stress(virial_bias) / volume`.

`Atoms('H2', positions=...)` is constructed without a cell, so `pbc.any()` is `False` and `cell.rank` is 0. In the diff's implementation this causes `volume = 1.0` and `unbiased_stress = np.zeros(6)` (EMT raises an error for stress on a non-periodic system), so `stress` is just the raw PLUMED bias virial unnormalized by any volume. The subsequent assertions — `stress.shape == (6,)` and `not np.allclose(stress, 0)` — can pass while testing a physically meaningless quantity. To be meaningful, this test should set a proper periodic cell (e.g. `cell=10.0 * np.eye(3), pbc=True`) so that the stress is well-defined. The edge-case of no cell should be covered by a separate test that verifies a `PropertyNotImplementedError` is raised.

The tolerance `abs=1e-10` is extremely tight. Per project coding standards, tolerances as tight as `1e-6` have caused spurious CI failures due to floating-point variance across platforms. For a comparison of floating-point stress values accumulated through multiple independent computation paths (EMT stress + zero bias contribution), prefer `abs=1e-5` or verify empirically across all target platforms before committing to a tighter bound.

Three issues: (1) the file is missing a trailing newline (the diff shows `\ No newline at end of file`); (2) the file path in parentheses `(ase/calculators/plumed.py)` should be a Sphinx cross-reference such as `:mod:`~ase.calculators.plumed`` so the changelog renders as a hyperlink; (3) the entry is missing the required MR reference at the end of the bullet, e.g. `(:mr:`NNNN`)`. All three are required by ASE's changelog guidelines.

general_comments.comment: There is no test that directly validates the analytical stress against a numerical finite-difference stress (e.g. using `calculate_numerical_stress` from `ase.calculators.fd`). The PR description states the implementation was tested this way, but the validation is absent from the submitted test suite. A round-trip test comparing numerical and analytical stress is the only reliable way to catch sign errors, unit errors, or off-diagonal symmetry bugs in the virial → stress conversion path. This test should be added before merging.

There is no test verifying that requesting stress on a system without a 3D periodic cell raises `PropertyNotImplementedError`. Without such a test, the boundary between a supported configuration (3D cell, `cell.rank == 3`) and an unsupported one (molecule, 2D slab) is unspecified and can silently regress. A dedicated test such as `with pytest.raises(PropertyNotImplementedError): atoms.get_stress()` on a non-3D system would pin this contract.

`compute_energy_and_forces` is a core internal computation method that is not part of the documented public API; the only public entry point is `calculate()`. It should be renamed to `_compute_energy_and_forces` (or a similarly private name) to signal that external callers should not rely on it, make the public surface area explicit, and be consistent with ASE's convention of prefixing internal helpers with `_`. The existing method `compute_bias` which is called directly in unit tests is an exception that could be documented as intentionally public for testability.
